the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

А вдруг... = what if. Core Russian adv meaning 'suddenly; all of a sudden' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level?

examples.text: Почему он вдруг сравнялся? Мы шли впереди на десять процентов!
examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level? We were ten percent ahead!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come back, to return', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'wine' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And what about the wine and fruit?

examples.text: Смотри, это электрогитара для Лёши. А тебе я взял чилийское вино и ягоды.
examples.trans: Look, this is an electric guitar for Lyosha. And for you I brought Chilean wine and berries.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'yesterday' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stupid, silly, foolish').

examples.trans: Vanya, are you stupid? Why did you just say that in front of him?

злиться.gloss: to be angry, to get mad

meanings.en: to be angry, to get mad
meanings.note: Злиться на кого + accusative. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be angry, to get mad', paired with 'разозлиться'.

examples.text: А знаешь, почему ты так злишься?

examples.text: Запомните: зло всегда возвращается к правителю.

meanings.note: A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

+ genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'because of; from behind' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: + dative: 'позвони мне' = call me. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'звонить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to phone', paired with 'звонить'.

meanings.note: Всё получилось = it all worked out. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn out, to work out', paired with 'получаться'.

examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?
